newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA STOCKS SEEN WEAK ON RATES, MARGIN RULES.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA STOCKS SEEN WEAK ON RATES, MARGIN RULES.

text.p: Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad's statement that a current policy of maintaining tight rupiah supply would be eased gradually is likely to bolster sentiment on the Jakarta bourse on Friday although selling pressure is likely to persist, brokers said.

Mar'ie made the comments after a surprise visit to the exchange on Thursday as the market plunged on accumulated concern over higher interest rates, new margin finance regulations and payments due on large rights issues.
"The visit would help bolster sentiment, but the market is likely to remain under selling pressure," one broker said.
On Thursday, the composite index ended down 21.92 points, or 3.13 percent, at 677.94 points.
